extracted.intended_audience: Offerors/prospective contractors and other applicants responding to the ONR BAA (contract and other transaction applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation-related standards for preparing and submitting full proposals under the Office of Naval Research BAA, including required documents, certifications, compliance with federal statutes/regulations, reporting obligations, and submission/format rules. Covers responsibilities for disclosure, conflicts of interest, safety/security surveys, and cost/certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying disclosure certification / SF-LLL
rubrics_metrics.description: If any funds other than Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to any person for influencing or attempting to influence a Federal officer or employee in connection with the Federal contract, grant, loan, or cooperative agreement, the applicant shall complete and submit Standard Form-LLL, 'Disclosure Form to Report Lobbying,' in accordance with its instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant shall require that the language of this certification be included in the award documents for all subawards at all tiers. This certification is a material representation under 31 U.S.C. 1352; failure to file may result in a civil penalty of $10,000 to $100,000 per failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re: prohibition on internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submission of its proposal or application, the applicant represents that it does not require any of its employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements or statements prohibiting or otherwise restricting those employees, contractors, subrecipients from lawfully reporting that waste, fraud, or abuse to a designated investigative or law enforcement representative of a Federal department or agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17 certifies to this statement and that statements are true, complete and accurate; false statements may subject signatory to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (18 U.S.C. §1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re: disclosure of funding sources (Section 223, FY2021 NDAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the proposing entity certifies compliance with Section 223(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA FY2021: (a) PI and key personnel certify that current and pending support provided is current, accurate and complete; (b) agree to update disclosure at agency request prior to award and during award term; (c) PI and key personnel have been made aware of requirements under Section 223(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17 certifies to this; false statements may have penalties (18 U.S.C. §1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Conflict of Interest (COI) disclosure requirement (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for assistance are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c), Codes of Conduct, to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in the award and administration of any contracts by which a recipient or subrecipient purchases property or services supported by federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You and your organization must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest to ONR. You must also disclose any potential or actual conflict(s) of interest for any identified subrecipient included in the application. ONR may request additional information and may request a conflict of interest mitigation plan, subject to ONR approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific conflict of interest – disclosure of collaborations and current/pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific collaborations on research and development projects should be considered when considering potential conflicts of interest. The potential conflict is mitigated by the disclosure of these collaborations and the list of current and pending support for senior and key researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must include in the list of current and pending support all collaborators, even if they did not formally provide support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for basic research awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals funded as basic research, ONR may utilize peer reviewers from academia, industry, and Government agencies to assist in periodic appraisal of performance under awards, as outlined in ONR Instruction 3966.1A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers who are not U.S. Government employees must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving full/partial copies of proposals and reports. Offerors may include travel costs for the PI to attend peer review. Peer reviews may consider information derived from project or program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance equipment/services (Public Law 115-232, Sec.889)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from obligating or expending loan or grant funds to procure/obtain, extend/renew contracts to procure/obtain, or enter/extend/renew contracts to procure equipment, services, or systems that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as substantial/essential components or critical technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered telecommunications equipment includes equipment produced by Huawei, ZTE (and subsidiaries/affiliates). For public safety, security, and surveillance purposes, also includes Hytera, Hangzhou Hikvision, and Dahua (and subsidiaries/affiliates). Also covers services provided by such entities or using such equipment and equipment/services from entities the Secretary of Defense reasonably believes are owned/controlled by a covered foreign country. See 2 CFR 200.216/200.471 and Public Law 115-232, section 889 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency assistance to transition away from covered telecom equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: In implementing the prohibition under section 889(f)(1), heads of executive agencies shall prioritize available funding and technical support to assist affected businesses, institutions and organizations as reasonably necessary to transition from covered communications equipment and services, procure replacement equipment and services, and ensure communications service is sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are expected to provide prioritized funding/technical support where necessary for transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of post-award reporting (Award Term: Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any Federal award may include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the post award reporting requirements (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII) are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters for specific reporting obligations and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of matters related to recipient integrity and performance (threshold $10,000,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total value of your currently active grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts from all Federal awarding agencies exceeds $10,000,000 at any time during the period of performance of this Federal award, you must maintain currency of information reported to SAM/FAPIIS about civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings described in the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is statutory under 41 U.S.C. 2313. All information posted to the designated system on/after April 15, 2011 (except past performance reviews required for Federal procurement contracts) will be publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proceedings that must be reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Report proceedings that: (a) are in connection with award/performance of a Federal award; (b) reached final disposition during the most recent five-year period; and (c) are: (i) criminal proceeding resulting in conviction; (ii) civil proceeding with finding of fault and payment of monetary fine/penalty/restitution/damages of $5,000 or more; (iii) administrative proceeding resulting in finding of fault and payment of a monetary fine/penalty of $5,000+ or reimbursement/restitution/damages over $100,000; or (iv) any other proceeding that could have led to the outcomes above or had disposition by consent/compromise with acknowledgment of fault, provided reporting does not conflict with laws/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the criteria in paragraph 2 of the award term to determine reportability and ensure reporting does not conflict with applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting procedures for integrity/performance matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter required information about each proceeding in the SAM Entity Management area as SAM requires. Do not submit the information a second time under assistance awards if already provided through SAM for procurement contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SAM data-entry requirements; SAM/FAPIIS is the authoritative repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting frequency for integrity/performance matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients subject to the requirement must report proceedings information through SAM for the most recent five-year period, either to report new information or affirm no new information. Recipients with cumulative Federal awards over $10,000,000 must disclose semiannually any information about criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain currency of SAM entries and perform semiannual updates if threshold exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to reporting (administrative proceeding, conviction, total value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: (a) Administrative proceeding — non-judicial adjudicatory process to determine fault/liability (e.g., SEC admin proceedings, CBCA, ASBCA), includes Federal/State proceedings only in connection with performance of a Federal contract/grant; excludes audits, site visits, corrective plans, inspection of deliverables. (b) Conviction — judgment/conviction by any court, including nolo contendere pleas. (c) Total value of currently active awards includes only Federal share of funding with recipient cost share, and value of expected funding increments/options even if not exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to interpret the reporting obligations in the award term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete proposal package required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal package must include: (1) Cover page (pdf); (2) Proposal Checklist (pdf); (3) Technical Proposal Template (word); (4) Cost Proposal Template (Excel) for prime and all proposed subcontractors; (5) DCAA Pre-award Survey of Prospective Contractor Accounting System Checklist (pdf) for contractors without approved accounting systems; (6) Statement of Work (SOW) (word); (7) ONR Contract Specific Representations and Certifications (pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–6 are located at ONR's submission webpage and contain instructions. FedConnect will not accept a proposal package unless the Cover Sheet is included. Attachments can be incorporated into the Proposal Checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements for proposal attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper Size: 8.5 x 11-inch paper; Margins: 1 inch; Spacing: single or double-spaced; Font: Times New Roman, 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to these formatting rules for attachments; nonconforming format may cause issues in processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of technical data/computer software rights (intellectual property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must submit a separate list of all technical data or computer software that will be furnished to the Government with other than unlimited rights with the proposal checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government will assume unlimited rights if offerors fail to identify any intellectual property restrictions. Include all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, and/or deliverables; if none, state 'NONE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified acquisition threshold proposals (≤ $250K) document requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals below the simplified acquisition threshold (≤ $250K), the Technical Proposal Template and Proposal Checklist documents, and the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet are required. Purchase orders can contain options as long as base+all options ≤ $250K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the reduced-document guidance for small-value proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract/inter-organizational transfer cost proposal requirement (>$250K)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed subcontracts or inter-organizational transfers over $250K, Offerors must provide a separate fully completed Cost Proposal Spreadsheet in support of the proposed costs. This spreadsheet and supporting documentation must be provided with the prime’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subcontract information is proprietary, it can be submitted via e-mail to the Program Officer listed on the Cover Page. Email must identify proposal title, prime Offeror, indicate the attachment is a subcontract, and describe subcontractor effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document file format and secure pdf-compatible requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents except the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet and Statement of Work Template must be submitted in a secure, pdf-compatible format. The Cost Proposal Spreadsheet must be submitted in a Microsoft Excel compatible format and the Statement of Work Template in Microsoft Word format. All attachments must be in secure, pdf-compatible format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure pdf-compatible format is intended to prevent unauthorized editing; a password should not be required to open the proposal. Amended proposals should follow the same guidance as the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options pricing and spreadsheet separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed options identified but not fully priced out in the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet will not be included in any resulting contract or other transaction agreement. If proposing options, they must be separately priced and separate spreadsheets should be provided for the base period and each option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a summary by period (base and options) and a breakdown of cost for each task in the Statement of Work. The sum of all costs by task worksheets MUST equal the total cost summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excel cost spreadsheet 'useable condition' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Excel spreadsheet should be in a 'useable condition' to aid the Government with its evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useable condition means the spreadsheet should visibly include and separately identify within each appropriate cell any and all inputs, formulas, calculations, etc. Do not provide 'value only spreadsheets' similar to a hard copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost breakdown by task requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a breakdown of cost for each task identified in the Statement of Work; the sum of all costs by task worksheets must equal the total cost summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal consistency between task worksheets and the overall cost summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed fee guidance and contract risk factor weighting (DFARS 215.404-71 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Objective for fixed fees is set in accordance with DFARS 215.404-71. Assign weights (percentage) to elements (e.g., Technical, Management/Cost Control) according to their input to total performance risk; total weights equal 100%. Assign a weighting score relative to the Risk Factor. Normal ranges and normal values are provided (e.g., Technical 3–7%, Management/Cost Control 3–7%, Normal Value 5% etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology Incentive (TI) is rarely utilized at ONR and requires strong and convincing justification; typical fee range on ONR contracts is 5% to 7.5%.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect registration and account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is utilizing FedConnect for submission of full proposals for contracts/other transaction agreements. To register: obtain a DUNS number (enter Company DUNS), register with SAM (SAM.gov), and if first to register in FedConnect your SAM MPIN will be required. Then create a FedConnect account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FedConnect how-to guide is available. Use provided FedConnect support contacts if needed. Do not use the FedConnect Message Center to submit questions to ONR; email the POCs in Section G instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect assistance contact and FAQ guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: FedConnect Support Team contact: fcsupport@fedconnect.net, Phone: 1-800-899-6665, Hours M–F 8 a.m.–8 p.m. EDT. FedConnect FAQs are on the ONR website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these support channels for technical assistance with FedConnect. Use ONR POCs for solicitation-specific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient qualifications / responsibility standard (FAR 9.104-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall be awarded to responsible prospective contractors only. See FAR 9.104-1 for the general standards against which an applicant will be assessed to determine responsibility. Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submission to assist the Contracting Officer’s evaluation of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide requested information to help the Contracting Officer determine responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS check and use in responsibility determination
rubrics_metrics.description: FAPIIS (Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System) will be checked prior to making an award. Applicants may comment in FAPIIS on any information entered by a federal government official. The information in FAPIIS will be used to judge entity integrity, business ethics, and record of performance that may affect determination of qualification to receive an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure relevant performance/integrity information is accurate and consider commenting in FAPIIS if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and negotiation of Government Furnished Equipment/Facilities (GFE/GFF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government research facilities and operational military units are available and should be considered as potential government-furnished equipment/facilities. These resources are of high value and in demand; it is unlikely all facilities would be used for any one program. Use of these facilities will be negotiated as the program unfolds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should indicate in the Proposal Checklist, Section II, Block 9, which facilities are critical for the project's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E) safety and preaward survey requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors proposing to use ammunitions and/or explosives under the research effort must comply with DoD manual 4145.26-M (DoD Contractor’s Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives) and obtain a preaward safety survey per DFARS PGI 223.370-4(C)(iv). The Offeror is solely responsible for contacting the cognizant DCMA office and obtaining the required preaward safety survey before proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required preaward safety surveys with proposal submissions. If Government will provide GFE A&E containing nitrocellulose-based propellants or nitrate ester-based materials, NMCARS 5252.223-9000 applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preaward security survey and AA&E security procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If AA&E are to be utilized, the Government requires a preaward security survey per DoD manual 5100.76-M. The Offeror may be required to have perimeter fencing and must provide written AA&E accountability procedures in accordance with DoD 5100.76-M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offeror should provide required preaward security survey and AA&E accountability procedures with proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of SAM FAR clauses (FAR 52.204-7 and 52.204-13)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.204-7 System for Award Management and FAR 52.204-13 System for Award Management Maintenance are incorporated into this BAA; FAR 52.204-13 will be incorporated in all awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with SAM registration and maintenance requirements as reflected in these FAR clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment Eligibility Verification (E-Verify) requirement (FAR 52.222-54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of FAR-based procurement contracts must enroll as Federal Contractors in E-Verify and use E-Verify to verify employment eligibility of all employees assigned to the award. All resultant contracts will include FAR 52.222-54, 'Employment Eligibility Verification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must be prepared to perform E-Verify checks on employees assigned to the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI (Organizational Conflict of Interest) disclosure statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An offeror shall state in its proposal whether they are aware of any information bearing on the existence of any actual or potential OCI as defined in FAR 2.101 and FAR Subpart 9.5 for itself and any proposed subcontractors, partners, consultants or affiliates. Offerors performing SETA for ONR are considered to have an OCI that may not be susceptible to mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nondisclosure or misrepresentation of an interest creating an OCI may result in disqualification or termination and other remedies (see 18 U.S.C. §1001 and 31 U.S.C. §3802(a)(2)). Offerors who do not provide support services to ONR or conclude no OCI exists shall include a specified certification statement in the proposal. Offerors who do provide support services or are aware of possible unfair competitive advantage shall submit detailed OCI information and a Mitigation Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, a Mitigation Plan shall: (i) provide organizational charts showing structure related to performance and relevant contracts; (ii) demonstrate how elements creating the OCI will be isolated from resources performing the work; (iii) show whether elements will be geographically/physically separated; (iv) describe process for reassigning personnel and restrictions; (v) describe controls including nondisclosure agreements over future employment of departing employees; (vi) describe OCI training offered/required, including timing, frequency, length, content; (vii) provide evidence of facts/circumstances that mitigate/ address OCI concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to FAR Subpart 9.5 for policies/procedures for avoiding, neutralizing, or mitigating OCIs. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer review and possible OCI-related remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer will review offeror certifications, statements, and OCI Mitigation Plans and may require additional information. If an OCI is found to exist, the Government may: (1) impose conditions to avoid the conflict, (2) disqualify the offeror, (3) award with appropriate mitigation conditions, or (4) seek a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Contracting Officer determines an actual/significant potential OCI exists that cannot reasonably be avoided, neutralized or mitigated, the offeror will be ineligible for award. Failure to disclose required OCI information results in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions and clauses applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of FAR, DFARS, and NMCARS provisions and clauses may be applicable to ONR contracts (e.g., 52.204-7, 52.215-20, 52.216-1, 52.217-9, 252.204-7012, 252.204-7019/7020, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to include any relevant and current FAR, DFARS or NMCARS clauses necessary and required in the final award. Offerors should be prepared to comply with applicable clauses listed and others the Government may include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data requirement (TINA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals submitted under this BAA that meet the TINA threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data. Offerors are required to execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable, but no later than five business days after the date of price agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cost or pricing data are submitted after price agreement, they will be reviewed after award to determine whether certified data submitted up to agreement was defective and whether the Government is entitled to a price adjustment under FAR 52.215-10 or 52.215-11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract authority for development/demonstration of prototypes (10 U.S.C. 2302e)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may award or modify a contract issued under this BAA to contain a contract line item or contract option for development and demonstration or initial production of technology developed under the contract or delivery of initial/additional items if created as result of work performed under the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority is in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2302e (Section 861 NDAA FY2018 as amended by Section 831 NDAA FY2021). Offerors should be aware of potential contract options for prototype development/initial production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced security controls on select defense industrial base partner networks
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may require enhanced security controls on select Defense Industrial Base partner networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific implementation and applicability details are provided elsewhere in ONR addenda/requirements; offerors should be prepared to meet enhanced security controls if applicable.
